issues.legal_issue: A court may permit a claim for possession to be added during execution of a decree for specific performance and grant possession without requiring a separate suit when possession is incidental to completing the conveyance and the person in possession is bound by the decree.
material_facts: The purchasers obtained a decree for specific performance of an agreement to sell immovable property, but possession had not been specifically claimed in the plaint.
A subsequent purchaser who was in possession was made a party to the decree and was directed to join in executing the sale deed.
During the suit, the subsequent purchaser had raised construction on the property and had undertaken to demolish it and restore the land if the suit succeeded.
The decree-holders sought possession in execution, and the High Court granted it despite the absence of an express possession claim in the original plaint.
issues.conclusion: The omission to claim possession in the plaint did not prevent the court from granting possession in execution. The court could permit an amendment to include that relief at the execution stage, and a separate suit was not required in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22(1)–(2) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, is a rule of pleading intended to avoid multiplicity of suits; its proviso permits amendment to include possession at any stage of the proceedings, and “proceedings” includes execution proceedings. In an appropriate case, possession is inherent in specific performance because a seller must give possession as required by section 55(1) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Sections 28(3)–(4) of the Specific Relief Act also contemplate further relief, including delivery of possession, in the same suit and bar a separate suit for relief claimable there. The court approved the approach in Rameshwar Nath v. Uttar Pradesh Union Bank, AIR 1956 All. 586; Mahender Nath Gupta v. M/s. Moti Ram Rattan Chand, AIR 1975 Delhi 155; and M/s. Ex-Servicemen Enterprises (P) Ltd. v. Sumey Singh, AIR 1976 Delhi 56, and relied additionally on Hungerford Investment Trust Ltd. v. Haridas Mundhra, AIR 1972 SC 1826, regarding the court’s continuing control over a specific-performance decree.

rule.if: specific_performance_execution_case and possession_not_claimed_initially and occupant_bound_by_decree and possession_incidental_to_conveyance and not independent_third_party_possession_right

predicates.specific_performance_execution_case: The proceeding seeks to execute a decree requiring specific performance of an agreement to transfer immovable property.
predicates.possession_not_claimed_initially: The claimant did not include a specific claim for possession in the original pleading.
predicates.occupant_bound_by_decree: The person in possession is a party bound by the decree, rather than an independent person outside it.
predicates.possession_incidental_to_conveyance: Giving possession is part of completing the transfer required by the decree.
predicates.independent_third_party_possession_right: A person outside the decree has an independent right to possession that would require separate relief.

issues.definition: When execution concerns specific performance, possession was omitted initially, possession is incidental to the conveyance, and the occupant is bound by the decree rather than holding an independent third-party right, possession relief may be added and granted in execution.
